description: I'm a technology consultant and software developer with experience in AI, data analytics and digital solutions. Our team is building SeasonsUg, using NASA Earth observation data to help farmers explore crop rotation strategies. We're looking for people with skills in agronomy, Earth science, geospatial analysis, UI/UX and software development.
summary:
SeasonsUg is a web-based decision-support application that helps farmers and agricultural extension officers make better-informed crop rotation decisions using NASA environmental data, soil information, crop characteristics and farmer priorities.

Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, the application brings together historical rainfall and temperature records, terrain information and crop requirements to help users compare alternative crop sequences across three growing seasons. Farmers can define field conditions and planning priorities, explore different rotation options, and understand the factors influencing each assessment.

The application uses NASA POWER climate data and incorporates NASA SRTM terrain information, alongside crop guidance and soil-related inputs. Its initial demonstration focuses on Namulonge, Uganda, where changing rainfall patterns and seasonal uncertainty make agricultural planning increasingly difficult.

Rather than predicting guaranteed harvests, SeasonsUg presents evidence, trade-offs and limitations in an understandable format. Its goal is to make satellite-informed agricultural planning more accessible, practical and useful to farmers and extension officers.
details:
What the project does

SeasonsUg is a crop rotation planning application designed to help farmers and agricultural extension officers evaluate planting decisions using environmental evidence and practical crop management considerations.

The project addresses the challenge of translating satellite observations and agricultural information into decisions that farmers can understand and act upon. Its initial implementation focuses on Namulonge, Uganda, with exploratory support for other locations.

How it works

Users create a field profile by specifying their location, previous crops, soil conditions, water availability and farming priorities.

The application combines this information with NASA climate records, crop characteristics and available soil and terrain information to assess alternative crop rotations across three growing seasons.

Its main capabilities include:

  • Field profiles capturing location, crop history and soil conditions.
  • An eight-crop catalogue covering maize, common beans, soybean, groundnut, cowpea, sorghum, sweet potato and cassava.
  • Historical rainfall and temperature analysis using NASA POWER.
  • Comparison of alternative crop sequences using crop duration, rainfall suitability, botanical families, rotation diversity and farmer priorities.
  • Soil property estimates from ISRIC SoilGrids, with a recorded demonstration snapshot when the live service is unavailable.
  • Terrain assessment using NASA SRTM where numerical extraction is available.
  • A separate seven-day weather outlook for short-term field planning.
  • Assessment results, explanations, warnings and reports that support discussions between farmers and extension officers.

NASA Earthdata catalogue searches also identify relevant GPM IMERG, SMAP and Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 products. These sources are identified transparently as metadata or discovery integrations where numerical environmental measurements have not yet been incorporated into the assessment.

Technology and development

SeasonsUg was developed using React, TypeScript, Vite, Node.js and Express. The user interface uses Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui components and data visualisation libraries.

The application connects to environmental data services through APIs and uses a rule-based comparison engine to evaluate crop rotation alternatives.

NASA POWER provides historical climate information. NASA Earthdata supports satellite dataset discovery, while ISRIC SoilGrids and Open-Meteo provide supplementary soil and short-range weather information.

AI-assisted development tools helped with software implementation, interface development and documentation. An optional Gemini integration supports generating plain-language explanations from structured assessment results. The underlying crop comparison rules remain separate from AI-generated text.

Creativity and intended impact

SeasonsUg goes beyond displaying satellite data by connecting environmental evidence to practical planting choices.

Instead of producing a single unexplained recommendation, it enables users to compare alternatives, understand trade-offs, identify potential rotation problems and recognise information that requires local verification.

The application is designed to assist agricultural extension services and eventually support wider use by smallholder farmers.

Its intended impact is better-informed crop rotation planning, stronger awareness of rainfall and soil constraints, and improved access to Earth observation information.

Considerations and limitations

The team considered data reliability, geographic coverage, different growing seasons, crop availability, local agricultural knowledge and the accessibility of technical information to farmers.

NASA POWER provides regional historical estimates, not measurements taken directly on a farm. SoilGrids provides modelled soil estimates, not laboratory test results. Some satellite integrations remain at the catalogue-discovery stage.

SeasonsUg does not guarantee crop yields, predict future soil fertility or replace agricultural extension officers. It provides decision support that should be interpreted alongside local field observations and professional agricultural advice.
